info.desc: My Aim Is True is the debut album by Elvis Costello. It was recorded from late 1976 to early 1977 over six four-hour studio sessions at Pathway Studios in Holloway, London Borough of Islington. It was the first of five consecutive Costello albums produced by Nick Lowe. The backing band was made up of members of Clover, who were uncredited on the original release due to contractual difficulties. In 2003, VH1 named, My Aim Is True, the 80th greatest album of all time. In 2003, the album was ranked number 168 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of the 500 greatest .

podcast.body: A copy of Elvis Costello's "My Aim Is True" album on CD is cited as an example of a poor early CD remaster. This specific CD sounds "awful," characterized by significant background hiss, a lack of bass, and rolled-off trebles, due to the master tapes for vinyl being directly transferred to CD without proper remastering for the new format. "I have a copy of Elvis Costello's My Amus True album and it sounds awful."

podcast.body: Recorded by Declan McManus (before he adopted the name Elvis Costello) using accumulated sick days from his computer programmer job. The album was described as articulate, literate, and occasionally angry. His manager suggested he change his name to Elvis Costello. It was released on July 22, 1977. "That first record was called My Amos True and it came out July 22nd, 1977."

podcast.body: Recorded in fits and starts throughout 1976 and 1977, this debut album was made on a tight budget of about 2,000 pounds at the primitive Pathway Studios in London, which was equipped with an old eight-track tape machine. Due to financial constraints, most songs were recorded in just one or two takes with minimal overdubbing, and Costello used a "shrill sounding" guitar he admitted he didn't know how to set up properly. The original version was sonically challenging with hiss and imperfections, to the point of being "unbearable" on its first CD release. "Listening to the original version of My Amus True can be sonically challenging because of all the hits and recording imperfections, something that was almost unbearable on the first ever CD release of the album."

podcast.body: Released on September 22, 1977, on Stiff Records, this album was recorded on weekends, vacation days, and sick days from Costello's computer programming job at Elizabeth Arden. His backing band for this record was The Sham Rocks, whose real name was Clover, an American group living in London, minus their lead singer Huey Lewis. Despite his folk singer and rhythm and blues background, Costello was lumped into the burgeoning British punk scene due to his sneer, anger, and geekiness, offering a unique angry singer-songwriter perspective in a landscape dominated by groups and "lightweights" like James Taylor and Cat Stevens. "Declan's first album was recorded during weekends, vacation days, and sick days from the computer room at Elizabeth Arden."

podcast.body: This was Elvis Costello's debut album, recorded in late 1976 and early 1977 while he was still working as a computer operator at Elizabeth Arden cosmetics. The album's backing band, the American group Clover, was uncredited on the original release due to contractual issues. The head of Stiff Records, Jake Riviera, wanted to release something quickly to capitalize on the burgeoning punk scene, but Costello didn't have a band ready, leading Riviera to hire Clover for late-night sessions in a tiny Islington studio. "Now the members of Clover were never credited on the original release of that first album, my name is true because they had a contractual issue."

podcast.body: This was his Nick Lowe-produced debut album. During its recording, Costello was still holding down a mundane day job, commuting between sessions and his data entry clerk position at Elizabeth Arden offices. He had not yet formed a backing band, so for this LP, he was backed by members of the California band Clover. Stiff Records marketed the album as punk adjacent, but its sound ranged widely. It initially reached number 86 on the Billboard album chart, but after his infamous Saturday Night Live appearance, it soared into the top 40, peaking at number 32. "My Aim is True."

podcast.body: When Stiff Records signed Elvis Costello, they needed to release material quickly. Jake Riviera, head of Stiff, recruited the band Clover to provide energy and anger to Costello's acoustic, twangy demos at Pathway Studios. Everyone from Clover, except their lead singer, played on the debut album, with the band officially changing their name to The Shamrocks for the contract to avoid legal issues with another group named Clover.
